notes.title: Ongoing Update - Mid June
notes.content: [p]With the first weeks of release past, and the first major update, we continue to follow-up players remarks and various comments on the game, improving it as they come.[/p][p][/p][h2]Today's changes:[/h2][p][/p][p][b]Data[/b]: some Korean characters names were poorly written and have been changed following players remarks ([i]change[/i])[/p][p][b]Data[/b]: Korean boats are properly name ([i]no more 'Junks'[/i])[/p][p][b]Graphics[/b]: Kamons of 1st and 8th divisions were inverted ([i]fix[/i]).[/p][p][b]Gameplay[/b] : mostly for play balance, mainly in the field of logisitcs and naval combat.[/p][list][*][p]unsupplied militias will suffer more hits and vanish more quickly[/p][/*][*][p]Japanese 1st and 2nd divisions will do more looting on their initial turns (turn 1-24), allowing them to recruit more supply units[/p][/*][*][p]some of the large Bune ships have been strengthened (resitance and firepower)[/p][/*][*][p]Japanese naval commanders re-assigned more accurately[/p][/*][/list][p][/p]

notes.title: SGS IMJIN WAR FIRST POST-RELEASE UPDATE
notes.content:
Based on continued playtest and initial remarks of our customers, we have prepared our first post-release update, with the following new elements or actions

[h2]NEW CONTENT[/h2]
- Added many [b]new units for Ming China[/b], among which
[list]
[*] 	Guards for Beijing
[*] 	Frontier Troops
[*] 	Elite Arquebusier
[*] 	Grand General canon
[*] 	Culverine light field gun
[*] 	New Wei yuan pao gun-mortar
[*] 	Fujian heavy warship
[/list]
- Added[b] new events[/b] such as
[list]
[*] 	Maritime Trade events (for both side)
[*] 	Firearms purchase (Joeson can purchase firearms troops only after Ming intervention
[/list]

[h2]FIXED, IMPROVED OR ALTERED CONTENT[/h2]
- Changed some data that prevent generals to properly command in battle
- Changed combat values and/or life points of some units (Atakebune, Samurai Ashigarus, Ming Heavy Cavalry, some Jurchens)
- Changed picture of general Li Rusong to better reflect his age at time of this war
- Improved morale values of some units (e.g. Ming infantry morale increased by 1)
- Overall revision and change of all leaders in the game (to give a better balance, for both sides)
- Re-assigned one region that was wrongly in Chungcheong to Gyeongsang province.
- Forbid some strange Jurchens units placement.
- Full revision of the Chinese language version (proofread by native Chinese wargamer).

[h3]Special thanks[/h3] to our friend [b]Wang Wenqi[/b] who, in addition to Chinese language proofreading,  provided us good information on Ming China (and access to the book “[i]A Dragon’s Head and a Serpent’s Tail[/i]” which gives a lot of verified points on Ming art of war).

notes.title: The bloodiest war in East Asia in the 16th century
notes.content:
Travel back to the late 16th century in East Asia to play the grand strategic struggle between the Japanese Samurais and Joseon Korean and Ming Chinese forces. You will find in the field and at sea, attempting to conquer new lands or defending your realms.

Fight Historical Campaigns and scenarios, and choose the different starting points and key moments of the war. 
In this turn-based grand strategic simulation, you play the Japanese commanders attempting to cross (and conquer) Korea in order to capture China, or the initially surprised defenders trying to defend key cities and castles and block enemy advance until their superior navy cuts the supply lines. 

The game is a new grand production of the team that brought you [i]SGS Korean War[/i] and [i]SGS Taipings[/i], and you will enjoy a similar gameplay and design, but with many more new features to faithfully render that famous conflict.
